p.src: Now Zhou Yu was routed in a single crushing attack by the three forces of Guan Yu, Huang Zhong, and Wei Yan, whom Zhuge Liang had placed in ambush beforehand. Huang Gai and Han Dang hurriedly rescued him aboard a ship, but countless men of the fleet were lost. From afar Zhou Yu saw Xuande, Lady Sun, and all their carriages, horses, and attendants halted atop the hill—how could he not be enraged? His arrow wound had not yet healed; stirred by his fury, it burst open, and he fell senseless to the ground. His officers revived him, then put their ships about and fled. Kongming ordered that they not be pursued, and himself returned with Xuande to Jingzhou, where they celebrated and rewarded the officers.

p.src: Zhou Yu returned to Chaisang. Jiang Qin and the rest of his company returned to Nanxu to report to Sun Quan. Sun Quan was overcome with rage and wished to appoint Cheng Pu commander-in-chief and raise an army to seize Jingzhou. Zhou Yu also submitted a memorial requesting that troops be raised to avenge the humiliation. Zhang Zhao remonstrated, “You must not. Cao Cao thinks day and night of avenging his defeat at Red Cliffs; it is only because he fears that Sun and Liu are united that he has not dared to raise an army. If, in a moment of anger, my lord now turns upon and seeks to devour an ally, Cao Cao will surely attack while we are exposed, and the state will be imperiled.” Gu Yong said, “Surely the capital at Xu has spies here. If Cao Cao learns that Sun and Liu are at odds, he will certainly send someone to win Liu Bei over. Fearing Eastern Wu, Liu Bei will inevitably submit to Cao Cao. If that happens, when will the Southland ever know peace? The best plan at present is to send someone to the capital at Xu with a memorial recommending Liu Bei as governor of Jingzhou. When Cao Cao learns of it, he will grow fearful and dare not send troops against the southeast. It will also keep Liu Bei from resenting my lord. Then we may send a trusted agent to sow discord, setting Cao and Liu against each other; we can take advantage of the opening and pursue our own designs. That would be the proper course.” Sun Quan said, “Yuanzhan’s counsel is excellent. But who can serve as our envoy?” Gu Yong replied, “There is a man here whom Cao Cao respects and admires; he can undertake the mission.” Sun Quan asked who it was. Gu Yong said, “Hua Xin is here. Why not send him?” Sun Quan was delighted and at once sent him to carry the memorial to the capital at Xu. Hua Xin accepted the command, set out, and went straight to the capital at Xu to seek an audience with Cao Cao. Hearing that Cao Cao had assembled his ministers in Ye Commandery to celebrate the Bronze Bird Terrace, Hua Xin proceeded there to await an audience.

p.src: Ever since his defeat at Red Cliffs, Cao Cao had constantly thought of vengeance; but suspecting that Sun and Liu would join forces, he dared not advance rashly. In the spring of the fifteenth year of Jian’an, the construction of the Bronze Bird Terrace was completed. Cao Cao therefore assembled all his civil and military officers in Ye Commandery and held a banquet in celebration. The terrace directly overlooked the Zhang River. In the center stood the Bronze Bird Terrace; to its left was the Jade Dragon Terrace and to its right the Golden Phoenix Terrace, each a hundred feet high. Two bridges spanned the heights and linked them together; amid a thousand gates and myriad chambers, gold and azure gleamed against each other.

p.src: That day Cao Cao wore a gold crown set with jewels, a green brocade robe, a jade belt, and pearl-studded shoes, and sat aloft. The civil and military officers stood in attendance below the terrace. Wishing to watch the military officers test their archery, Cao Cao ordered an attendant to hang a red brocade battle robe from Xichuan upon a drooping willow branch, set up an archery target below it, and mark off a distance of one hundred paces. He divided the military officers into two teams. All members of the Cao clan wore red, while the other officers and soldiers wore green. Each bore a carved bow and fine arrows, mounted and reined his horse, and awaited orders. Cao Cao issued an order: “Whoever can strike the red center of the target shall be awarded the brocade robe. Whoever misses shall be fined a cup of water.” The order had scarcely been given when a young general galloped out from the red-robed team. The onlookers saw that it was Cao Xiu. Cao Xiu galloped back and forth three times, nocked an arrow, drew his bow to the full, and loosed; the shaft struck the red center squarely. Gongs and drums sounded together, and all raised a cheer. Seeing this from the terrace, Cao Cao was delighted and said, “He is the thousand-li colt of my clan!” Just as he was about to have someone fetch the brocade robe for Cao Xiu, a rider suddenly dashed from the green-robed team and cried, “The prime minister’s brocade robe ought first to be won by one of us outside his clan; his own kinsmen should not push ahead of others.”

p.src: Cao Cao looked and saw that the man was Wen Ping. The officers said, “Let us see Wen Zhongye’s archery.” Wen Ping took up his bow, spurred his horse, and loosed an arrow, which also struck the red center. All cheered as gongs and drums sounded in a tumult. Wen Ping shouted, “Quickly, bring me the robe!” But another general galloped out from the red-robed team and cried sternly, “Wenlie shot first. How dare you contend for the prize? Watch me settle the matter between you two with an arrow!” He drew his bow to the full and shot; his arrow also struck the red center. The crowd cheered in unison. They looked and saw that it was Cao Hong. Cao Hong was about to take the robe when yet another general emerged from the green-robed team, raised his bow, and called, “What is remarkable about the archery of you three? Watch me shoot!” The onlookers saw that it was Zhang He. Zhang He galloped his horse, twisted around, and shot backward; his arrow also struck the red center. All four arrows clustered together in the red center. Everyone exclaimed, “Fine archery!” Zhang He said, “The brocade robe should be mine!”

p.src: Before he had finished speaking, a general galloped out from the red-robed team and shouted, “What is so extraordinary about turning around to shoot backward? Watch me seize the red center with my shot!” The onlookers saw that it was Xiahou Yuan. Xiahou Yuan galloped to the boundary, wheeled around, and loosed an arrow that struck squarely amid the other four. Gongs and drums sounded together. Xiahou Yuan reined in his horse, lowered his bow, and shouted, “Is this shot enough to win the brocade robe?” At once a general rode out from the green-robed team and cried, “Leave that robe for me, Xu Huang!” Xiahou Yuan said, “What further feat of archery can you perform to take my robe?” Xu Huang replied, “There is nothing remarkable in striking the red center. Watch me take the brocade robe itself!” He took up his bow, nocked an arrow, and shot toward the distant willow switch; the arrow severed it cleanly, and the brocade robe fell to the ground. Xu Huang galloped over, snatched up the robe, donned it, then rode swiftly before the terrace and called out in salute, “My thanks for the robe, Prime Minister!” Cao Cao and all the officers praised and admired him. Just as Xu Huang reined in his horse to turn back, a green-robed general suddenly sprang out beside the terrace and shouted, “Where do you think you are taking that brocade robe? Leave it for me at once!” The onlookers saw that it was Xu Chu. Xu Huang said, “The robe is already mine. How dare you take it by force!” Xu Chu made no reply but galloped straight at him to seize the robe. As the two horses drew close, Xu Huang struck at Xu Chu with his bow. Xu Chu caught the bow with one hand and dragged Xu Huang from his saddle. Unable to free his bow, Xu Huang hastily twisted down from his horse; Xu Chu also dismounted, and the two seized each other and began to fight. Cao Cao hurriedly ordered men to separate them. By then the brocade robe had been torn to shreds. Cao Cao ordered both men to come up onto the terrace. Xu Huang glared with knitted brows, while Xu Chu ground his teeth; each still intended to fight the other. Cao Cao laughed and said, “I merely wished to behold the valor of you gentlemen. Would I begrudge a single brocade robe?” He then ordered all the generals to ascend the terrace and presented each with a bolt of Shu brocade. Each of the generals offered thanks. Cao Cao ordered everyone to sit according to rank. Music sounded in rivalry, and delicacies from land and water were arrayed together. Civil and military officers took turns offering cups, and toasts passed back and forth.

p.src: Cao Cao turned to the civil officers and said, “The military officers have taken their pleasure in mounted archery and fully displayed their might and valor. You gentlemen are all men of profound learning. Having ascended this lofty terrace, can you fail to offer fine compositions commemorating the splendid occasion?” The officers all bowed and said, “We shall gladly obey your command.”

p.src: At that time, Wang Lang, Zhong Yao, Wang Can, Chen Lin, and a group of civil officials presented poems of their own composition. Many lines in the poems extolled Cao Cao's towering achievements and virtue and implied that it was fitting for him to receive the Mandate. When Cao Cao had read them all, he laughed and said, “Your fine compositions praise me far too highly. I was originally a man of little wisdom or learning, first recommended to office as Filial and Incorrupt. Later, when the realm fell into great disorder, I built a retreat fifty li east of Qiao, intending to read in spring and summer and hunt with bow and arrow in autumn and winter, waiting until peace returned before entering public service. Unexpectedly, the court summoned me to serve as Commandant of the Army, so I changed my purpose and devoted myself to defeating rebels and winning merit for the state, hoping only that after my death the path to my tomb might bear the inscription, ‘Tomb of Lord Cao, the Late General Who Conquered the West under the Han.’ That would have fulfilled my life's ambition. Since taking the field against Dong Zhuo and suppressing the Yellow Turbans, I have eliminated Yuan Shu, defeated Lü Bu, destroyed Yuan Shao, and pacified Liu Biao's lands, thereby bringing peace to the realm. Now I am Chancellor, and have attained the highest rank possible for a subject. What more could I desire? Had the state been without me, who knows how many men would have proclaimed themselves emperor and how many king? Some see the weight of my authority, indulge in wild conjecture, and suspect me of disloyal ambitions. They are gravely mistaken. I often recall how Confucius praised King Wen's supreme virtue; those words remain ever bright in my heart. But if it is demanded that I relinquish my troops and retire to the fief and office of Marquis of Wuping, that I truly cannot do. For I sincerely fear that the moment I surrender military command, someone will do me harm; and if I fall, the state itself will be imperiled. Therefore I cannot court an empty reputation only to incur a real calamity. Surely none of you fully understands my mind.” They all rose and bowed, saying, “Even Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou could not equal Your Excellency the Chancellor.” A later poet wrote:

p.src: Cao Cao drank several cups in succession and became thoroughly intoxicated. He called for his attendants to bring brush and inkstone, intending to compose a poem on the Bronze Bird Terrace himself. He had only just set brush to paper when a report suddenly came: “Hua Xin, envoy from the Southland, has memorialized the throne to appoint Liu Bei Governor of Jingzhou. Sun Quan has given his younger sister to Liu Bei in marriage, and more than half of the nine commanderies along the Han River now belong to Liu Bei.” At the news, Cao Cao lost his composure and dropped the brush to the ground. Cheng Yu said, “Amid armies ten thousand strong, with arrows and stones raining upon you, Your Excellency has never been shaken; why, then, are you so alarmed now merely to hear that Liu Bei has gained Jingzhou?” Cao Cao replied, “Liu Bei is a dragon among men, but all his life he has never found the waters he needed. Now that he has gained Jingzhou, it is as though a confined dragon has entered the open sea. How could I remain unmoved?” Cheng Yu asked, “Does Your Excellency know why Hua Xin has come?” Cao Cao said, “I do not.” Cheng Yu said, “Sun Quan has always been wary of Liu Bei and wishes to attack him; but he fears that Your Excellency might strike while his lands stand empty. He therefore sent Hua Xin as envoy to recommend Liu Bei for office. His only purpose is to reassure Liu Bei and thwart Your Excellency's designs.”

p.src: Cao Cao nodded and said, “Indeed.” Cheng Yu continued, “I have a plan that will make the Sun and Liu houses turn upon and devour each other. Your Excellency may then seize the opportunity, and with a single assault destroy both enemies.” Cao Cao was delighted and asked him to explain the plan. Cheng Yu said, “The mainstay of the Southland is Zhou Yu. If Your Excellency now memorializes the throne to appoint Zhou Yu Administrator of Nanjun and Cheng Pu Administrator of Jiangxia, while detaining Hua Xin at court and granting him high office, Zhou Yu will inevitably make an enemy of Liu Bei. Would it not be an excellent course for us to act while they are locked in conflict?” Cao Cao said, “Zhongde's words accord perfectly with my own thoughts.” He accordingly summoned Hua Xin onto the terrace and bestowed lavish rewards upon him. When the banquet ended that day, Cao Cao led his civil and military officers back to Xuchang and memorialized the throne to appoint Zhou Yu chief Administrator of Nanjun and Cheng Pu Administrator of Jiangxia. He had Hua Xin appointed Minister of the Court of Judicial Review and kept him in the capital at Xu. When the imperial commission reached the Southland, Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu each accepted his appointment.

p.src: Once Zhou Yu had assumed command of Nanjun, his desire for revenge grew still stronger. He therefore wrote to the Marquis of Wu, requesting an order for Lu Su to go and demand the return of Jingzhou. Sun Quan accordingly said to Lu Su, “You once vouched for lending Jingzhou to Liu Bei. Now he keeps delaying its return. How long do you mean to wait?” Lu Su replied, “The written agreement states clearly that he will return it once he has gained the Western Riverlands.” Sun Quan rebuked him: “He talks only of taking the Western Riverlands, yet to this day has not even moved his troops. Are we to wait until everyone has grown old?” Lu Su said, “I am willing to go and speak to him.” He then embarked and made his way to Jingzhou.

p.src: Now Liu Bei and Kongming were in Jingzhou, gathering abundant grain and fodder and drilling their troops and horses; many worthy men from near and far came to join them. When word suddenly came that Lu Su had arrived, Liu Bei asked Kongming, “What is Zijing's purpose in coming here?” Kongming replied, “Sun Quan recently memorialized the throne to appoint you Governor of Jingzhou. That was a stratagem born of his fear of Cao Cao. Cao Cao appointed Zhou Yu Administrator of Nanjun because he wishes our two houses to destroy each other, allowing him to profit between us. Lu Su has come now because Zhou Yu, having accepted the office of Administrator, intends to demand Jingzhou from us once more.” Liu Bei asked, “How should I answer him?” Kongming said, “If Lu Su raises the matter of Jingzhou, my lord, you must burst loudly into tears. When your grief has reached its height, I shall come out and offer counsel.”

p.src: Their plan settled, they received Lu Su into the residence, exchanged the proper courtesies, and arranged their seats. Lu Su said, “Now that the Imperial Uncle has become a son-in-law of the Southland, he is my lord and master. How would I dare sit in his presence?” Liu Bei laughed and said, “Zijing, you and I are old friends. Why be so modest?” Only then did Lu Su take his seat. When the tea was finished, Lu Su said, “I come today under the solemn command of the Marquis of Wu, expressly on the matter of Jingzhou. The Imperial Uncle has occupied the province on loan for a long while, yet we have not had the honor of seeing it returned. Now that our two houses are joined by marriage, you should, for the sake of that kinship, hand it back without further delay.” Hearing this, Liu Bei covered his face and wept bitterly. Startled, Lu Su asked, “Why does the Imperial Uncle grieve so?” Liu Bei continued sobbing without cease. Kongming emerged from behind a screen and said, “I have been listening for some time. Zijing, do you know why my lord is weeping?” Lu Su replied, “I truly do not.” Kongming said, “It is not difficult to see. When my lord first borrowed Jingzhou, he promised to return it after taking the Western Riverlands. Yet on careful reflection, Liu Zhang of Yizhou is my lord's kinsman of a younger branch; both are of the blood of the Han imperial house. If he raises an army to seize Liu Zhang's cities, he fears that outsiders will spit upon his name; yet if he does not take them and returns Jingzhou, where can he find a place to shelter himself? But if he refuses to return it, he cannot face his honored brother-in-law. The matter truly leaves him caught between two impossible choices, and anguish wrings these tears from him.” When Kongming had finished, his words touched Liu Bei's deepest sorrow; Liu Bei truly beat his breast, stamped his feet, and wailed aloud. Lu Su consoled him, saying, “Imperial Uncle, set aside your distress for now and deliberate at length with Kongming.” Kongming said, “May I trouble you, Zijing, when you return to the Marquis of Wu, not to begrudge us a few words, but to explain earnestly all these painful circumstances and ask him to grant us a little more time.” Lu Su asked, “What are we to do if the Marquis of Wu refuses?” Kongming replied, “Since the Marquis of Wu has given his own younger sister in marriage to the Imperial Uncle, how could he refuse? I trust you, Zijing, to speak well of us when you make your reply.”

p.src: Lu Su was a generous and benevolent elder; seeing Xuande so grief-stricken, he could only consent. Xuande and Kongming bowed in gratitude. When the banquet ended, they escorted Lu Su to his boat. He went straight to Chaisang, met Zhou Yu, and related the whole affair. Zhou Yu stamped his foot and said, “Zijing, you have fallen for Zhuge Liang’s scheme yet again! When Liu Bei was dependent upon Liu Biao, he often harbored designs of annexation; how much more so with Liu Zhang of the Western Riverlands? If you keep letting them put us off like this, you yourself will inevitably be implicated. I have a plan that will keep Zhuge Liang from escaping my calculations. Zijing, you must make another journey.” Lu Su said, “I should like to hear your ingenious plan.” Zhou Yu said, “You need not go to see the Marquis of Wu. Return directly to Jingzhou and tell Liu Bei: ‘Since the houses of Sun and Liu are joined in marriage, they are now one family. If Lord Liu cannot bear to seize the Western Riverlands, we of Eastern Wu will raise an army and take them ourselves. Once we have won them, we shall make them the bride’s dowry, and you can then return Jingzhou to Eastern Wu.’” Lu Su said, “The Western Riverlands are far away, and taking them will be no easy matter. Might this plan of yours prove impracticable, Commander?” Zhou Yu laughed. “Zijing, you truly are an honest elder. Do you imagine I truly mean to conquer the Western Riverlands for him? I shall merely use that as a pretext. My true purpose is to seize Jingzhou while inducing him to make no preparations. When Eastern Wu’s forces pass through Jingzhou on their way to subdue the west, we shall ask him for money and provisions; Liu Bei will surely leave the city to welcome and reward the troops. We shall seize the moment to kill him and capture Jingzhou, avenging my grievance and relieving you of your peril.”

p.src: Lu Su was delighted and set out once more for Jingzhou. Xuande consulted with Kongming. Kongming said, “Lu Su cannot have gone to see the Marquis of Wu. He merely went to Chaisang and devised some scheme with Zhou Yu, and now he comes to lure us into it. Whatever he says, my lord need only watch for my nod and agree to everything.” Their plan settled, Lu Su entered and, after the courtesies, said, “The Marquis of Wu greatly praised the Imperial Uncle’s noble virtue. He then conferred with his generals and resolved to raise an army to conquer the Western Riverlands on the Imperial Uncle’s behalf. Once the Western Riverlands are taken, they will be exchanged for Jingzhou and provisionally counted as the bride’s dowry. We ask only that you supply some money and provisions when our troops pass through.” On hearing this, Kongming hastily nodded and said, “How kind of the Marquis of Wu!” Xuande raised his clasped hands in thanks and said, “This is all owing to Zijing’s good offices.” Kongming said, “When the mighty host arrives, we shall go far out to welcome and reward it.” Lu Su rejoiced inwardly and, when the banquet ended, took his leave and returned.

p.src: Xuande asked Kongming, “What does this mean?” Kongming laughed heartily. “Zhou Yu’s death is near! Such a scheme could not deceive even a child!” Xuande asked again how that could be. Kongming said, “This is the stratagem of ‘borrowing a road to destroy Guo.’ Conquering the Western Riverlands is the false pretext; seizing Jingzhou is the true aim. They mean to wait until my lord leaves the city to welcome their army, seize you when the opportunity presents itself, and then storm the city, attacking us unprepared and taking us by surprise.” Xuande said, “What are we to do?” Kongming said, “Set your mind at ease, my lord. Simply prepare a concealed bow to capture the fierce tiger and arrange fragrant bait to hook the giant turtle. When Zhou Yu arrives, even if he does not die, nine-tenths of his life will be gone.” He then summoned Zhao Yun and gave him his instructions: “Do thus and thus; I shall arrange everything else myself.” Xuande was overjoyed. p.src: Now Lu Su returned to Zhou Yu and reported that Xuande and Kongming were delighted and unsuspecting, and were preparing to leave the city to welcome the army. Zhou Yu laughed heartily. “So this time they have fallen for my scheme!” He ordered Lu Su to report to the Marquis of Wu and have Cheng Pu lead troops in support. By then Zhou Yu’s arrow wound had gradually healed and his body was sound. He appointed Gan Ning as vanguard, while he himself followed with Xu Sheng and Ding Feng in the second division; Ling Tong and Lü Meng formed the rear guard. A great force of fifty thousand by land and water advanced toward Jingzhou. Aboard his ship, Zhou Yu laughed from time to time, believing Kongming had fallen into his trap. When the vanguard reached Xiakou, Zhou Yu asked, “Has anyone from Jingzhou come ahead to meet us?” A man reported, “Imperial Uncle Liu has sent Mi Zhu to see the Commander.” Zhou Yu summoned him and asked about the arrangements for welcoming the army. Mi Zhu said, “My lord has made every preparation.” Zhou Yu said, “Where is the Imperial Uncle?” Mi Zhu said, “He awaits you at the gate of Jingzhou, to offer you a cup of wine.” Zhou Yu said, “We are setting out on this distant campaign for the sake of your house; the courtesies for rewarding the army must not be treated lightly.” Mi Zhu received this message and returned ahead of them.

p.src: Warships crowded the river, advancing one after another in formation. As they drew near Gong’an, there was neither a single warship nor anyone coming from afar to meet them. Zhou Yu urged the ships onward at speed. When they were a little over ten li from Jingzhou, the river lay utterly still and empty. The scouts returned and reported, “Two white banners fly atop Jingzhou’s walls, but not a single person can be seen.” Growing suspicious, Zhou Yu ordered the ships brought alongside the bank. He personally went ashore and mounted a horse, taking Gan Ning, Xu Sheng, Ding Feng, and the other officers with him, and led three thousand picked attendants straight toward Jingzhou. When they reached the foot of the walls, there was still no sign of movement. Zhou Yu reined in his horse and ordered his soldiers to call at the gate. Someone atop the wall asked who they were. The Wu soldiers replied, “It is Commander Zhou of Eastern Wu in person.” Before they had finished speaking, a wooden clapper suddenly sounded, and spears and swords were raised all along the walls. Zhao Yun appeared in the gate tower and said, “Commander, what is the true purpose of this expedition?” Zhou Yu said, “I am going to conquer the Western Riverlands for your lord. Can it be that you still do not know?” Zhao Yun said, “Military Adviser Kongming already knows of your stratagem of ‘borrowing a road to destroy Guo,’ and so he left Zhao Yun here. My lord has said: ‘Liu Zhang and I are both kinsmen of the imperial house of Han. How could I bear to betray righteousness and seize the Western Riverlands? If you of Eastern Wu truly conquer Shu, I shall let down my hair and retire into the mountains, rather than break faith with the world.’” When Zhou Yu heard this, he wheeled his horse about to return. Just then a man carrying a command banner rode up before him and reported, “Scouts have learned that four armies are attacking us at once: Guan Yu is advancing from Jiangling, Zhang Fei from Zigui, Huang Zhong from Gong’an, and Wei Yan by the narrow road from Yiling. No one knows how many troops the four armies contain. Their battle cries shake the country for over a hundred li around, and all are shouting that they mean to capture Zhou Yu.” Zhou Yu gave a great cry from horseback; his arrow wound burst open again, and he fell beneath his horse. Indeed:
